purpose: Offline contrasts for evidence-proportionate passive diagnostic advice; not model generations or a new runtime contract
authorship: Synthetic facts and source-derived expectations, implementation-assistant authored/reviewed; not blinded or externally graded
historical_scores: Unchanged; applying these criteria is a separate diagnostic review
common_rules: Accept technically equivalent wording and useful qualified recommendations; do not require an exact artifact name.
Counters are valid for their aggregate metric. Reject unsupported attribution to a specific exchange or drop cause, not the mere recommendation of counters.
Inspect a flow record's keys, observation point, time window, sampling and correlation granularity; a flow record is not automatically evidence for one particular packet.
A proposed artifact is not supplied evidence. Request it conditionally if available/authorized; never claim it was read or collected.
Preserve supported positive observations and modeled results while limiting conclusions to their actual scope.
No fixed requirement for application-response evidence when the question asks only for a modeled path or aggregate activity. Any claim actually made must be justified.

cases.title: Useful aggregate counters without exchange attribution
cases.question: Explain what these two interface samples establish about activity and transmission errors. Can they identify whether a particular DNS request was sent? Suggest one relevant passive artifact, without collecting anything.
establishes: Same-epoch deltas are 480000 output octets, 120 unicast transmission requests and 4 output errors over 60 seconds.
The interface counters show aggregate activity and errors; this is a valid diagnostic use.
unknown: Which traffic contributed each delta, whether the named DNS request appeared on the wire, and the cause of the errors.

passive_artifacts.artifact: Existing egress trace correlated with the DNS transaction and time
passive_artifacts.availability: Not supplied; request only if available and authorized
passive_artifacts.can: Show the matched packet at the trace's documented observation point
passive_artifacts.cannot: By itself establish remote application processing or make other interface errors specific to that exchange

cases.incorrect_example: The 120 additional output packets prove the DNS request left successfully, and the 4 errors prove ARP caused its loss.
minimum_criteria: Retain useful aggregate deltas without attributing them to one exchange.
Do not call ifHCOutUcastPkts an unconditional count of successful wire transmissions.
Keep the artifact a recommendation, not execution.

cases.title: Sampled ingress flow versus a positively matched egress trace
cases.question: For diagnostic datagram seq-214, compare what the interface counters, sampled ingress flow record and existing post-egress TAP trace actually establish. Which supports this specific datagram appearing on the outgoing link? Do any establish server processing or a reply? Recommend one passive artifact for the remaining gap. Use only the supplied records; do not execute reads, captures or tests.

source_records.observation_point: passive TAP on link after router egress

establishes: Counters show aggregate interface activity. The sampled flow records a selected matching-flow observation at ingress, without datagram identity.
The supplied TAP trace matches seq-214 and positively establishes that datagram's presence on the documented post-egress link in this synthetic scenario.
unknown: Server application acceptance, response generation and response arrival at the client; no such record is supplied.

passive_artifacts.artifact: Existing server request/response audit correlated by seq-214 and time
passive_artifacts.can: Distinguish documented application acceptance and response generation
passive_artifacts.cannot: Alone establish that a generated response reached the client's application

passive_artifacts.artifact: Existing reverse-direction trace or client receipt log with the transaction identifier
passive_artifacts.availability: Alternative request, not a required second artifact
passive_artifacts.can: Establish a matching response at its own observation point
passive_artifacts.cannot: Certify unrelated requests or future service health

cases.incorrect_example: The interface counters or sampled ingress flow prove seq-214 was transmitted successfully and answered by the server; alternatively, no actual egress conclusion is possible despite the matched TAP frame.
minimum_criteria: Differentiate all three artifacts rather than treating counters and flow records as interchangeable.
Accept the positively matched post-egress trace; do not suppress a justified conclusion.
Keep server processing and reply unresolved.
Give one useful permitted passive recommendation without execution; no exact wording required.

cases.title: A route and unrelated peering do not resolve the intended neighbor
cases.question: Does the supplied route, up port and established BGP peer settle next-hop address resolution in the services VRF? Identify the most relevant existing passive artifact to request; do not retrieve it.
establishes: A static route is selected and its recorded port is up.
The BGP session and guest-VRF neighbor are facts in different scopes.
unknown: The required services-VRF/interface neighbor binding and any particular packet's traversal.

passive_artifacts.artifact: Existing ARP/neighbor cache or recorded ARP exchange for the intended device, services VRF, interface and next hop
passive_artifacts.can: Establish a recorded binding/resolution exchange at its stated time
passive_artifacts.cannot: An installed static mapping alone does not demonstrate current reachability or application response

cases.incorrect_example: BGP Established, or a same-address neighbor in another VRF, proves the static route's Ethernet next hop is reachable.
minimum_criteria: Keep routing, protocol peering and link-layer resolution separate.
Preserve VRF/interface ownership; unavailable resolution is not proof of failed resolution.
Do not dismiss the valid route or invent a BGP fault.

cases.title: IPv6 STALE is not a missing mapping or a proven failure
cases.question: What does this IPv6 neighbor state establish, and what remains uncertain? Suggest one passive follow-up artifact without running a probe.
establishes: A recorded IPv6 link-layer mapping exists; STALE lacks recent positive reachability confirmation.
unknown: Current neighbor reachability, a specific packet's delivery and application response.

passive_artifacts.artifact: Existing scoped neighbor-state transitions or timestamped Neighbor Solicitation/Advertisement trace
passive_artifacts.availability: Not supplied; no new probe or capture authorized
passive_artifacts.can: Show a recorded later confirmation or transition and its time
passive_artifacts.cannot: Automatically establish application receipt, continuous health or the result of unobserved traffic

cases.incorrect_example: STALE proves the peer is down, so obtain an IPv4 ARP dump or run an active ping to repair it.
minimum_criteria: Retain the known mapping without relabeling STALE as failed or recently confirmed.
Use IPv6 ND semantics, not an IPv4 ARP remedy.
Recommend a passive record, not collection or repair.
cases.scope_note: Reasoning-only synthetic contrast; not a claim of new IPv6 simulator or reader support

cases.title: Healthy declared model versus unobserved application exchange
cases.question: The declared model delivers both directions. Does that establish an actual application reply? Recommend two distinct passive artifacts that could separate traversal from application behavior. Do not execute anything.
establishes: Both directions are supported under the declared modeled inputs; retain that positive result.
unknown: Whether query-602 traversed the real path, reached an application, produced a reply or was consumed by the client.

passive_artifacts.artifact: Existing scoped packet observation with query-602 identity and documented capture point
passive_artifacts.can: Distinguish presence of the matching traffic at that point
passive_artifacts.cannot: By itself prove application processing or observations beyond that point

passive_artifacts.artifact: Existing server request/response or client transaction audit for query-602
passive_artifacts.can: Document processing/generation or client acceptance as explicitly recorded
passive_artifacts.cannot: A server response-generation log alone proves neither network delivery nor client consumption

cases.incorrect_example: Both modeled directions delivered, so the application definitely replied; two generic counter snapshots prove the same thing.
minimum_criteria: Keep modeled delivery positive and scoped.
Separate traversal and application questions with two useful purposes.
Do not assume a proposed artifact already exists or was collected.

cases.title: Retain a positively recorded exchange without claiming universal health
cases.question: What parts of request req-312 and its response are established? What one passive artifact could address the remaining client-side gap? Use the supplied evidence without new execution.

source_records.source_scope: explicit server application audit in this synthetic scenario

establishes: The request is recorded on the outgoing link, server processing and response generation are explicitly audited, and a matching reply is observed at client ingress.
unknown: Whether the client application consumed the reply, other transactions and future service health.

passive_artifacts.artifact: Existing client application receipt/processing log correlated with req-312
passive_artifacts.can: Document consumption or a client-side error for this transaction
passive_artifacts.cannot: Certify all transactions or continuous service health

cases.incorrect_example: No delivery conclusion is possible because the whole exchange was merely modeled; or ingress arrival proves every client operation is healthy.
minimum_criteria: Preserve each explicitly supported positive recorded conclusion within the synthetic scenario.
Do not equate link observation with application consumption.
Use one relevant permitted passive recommendation; do not repeat proof already supplied.
